Prevention: Plow ratoon of the previous crop and destroy all off-season host plants such as rice ratoons and volunteers.
Plant early and synchronize planting with other rice fields.
Plant at wider spacing (because close spacing provides a suitable micro- environment for the gall midge survival).
Contact your local agriculture office for up-to-date lists of varieties available.
Encourage build up of biological control agents by reducing insecticide sprays.
Monitoring: Monitor fields regularly at weekly intervals.
Look for elongated tubular developing tillers and where possible presence of midge larvae or adults.
When populations appear to be increasing, check twice a week.
If population is high (>10% infection) then do direct control.
Direct Control: Use sticky board with oil or glue, place next to light near rice field to attract adult gall midges.
Spray insecticides to kill the adults when there’s an outbreak.
Restrictions: For all pesticide usage, follow instructions on product label.
